hypothesis: The selective exact actual-number rank kernel may have a batch-size-dependent throughput optimum on the hosted CI CPU. A fixed 4,096-formula synthetic sample processed by the same number-major score kernel and selective rank extraction, with candidate batch sizes 512,1024,2048,4096, will yield at least 1.25x throughput over the baseline full stable rank kernel at batch 1024 for at least one candidate size.

baseline.kernel: number-major scores 40xB plus stable full argsort for all 40 numbers; only the five actual-number ranks are extracted

candidate.kernel: unchanged number-major score matrix; exact selective actual-number rank against all 40 scores; stable lower-number tie-break

quantitative_acceptance.rank_parity_scope: five actual-number ranks for all 4,096 formulas at each candidate batch size; zero mismatches
quantitative_acceptance.selection_rule: select the batch size with maximum median formula throughput among the four preregistered sizes; if maximum speedup is below 1.25x, reject the optimization

strict_prior_and_leakage_guardrails.feature_state: all 27 features for each target i use draws[0:i] only
strict_prior_and_leakage_guardrails.target_use: target quintet is used only for metric extraction after the 40 number scores from prior-only features are computed
strict_prior_and_leakage_guardrails.tie_break: stable lower-number priority exactly matches full argsort
strict_prior_and_leakage_guardrails.selection: Discovery top-100 then one Validation freeze; Blind OOS excluded

limitations: this is a synthetic compute-performance experiment, not predictive evidence
no historic outcome, split metric, formula shortlist or blind target is used to select the batch size
full Q92 historical walk-forward and append-only persistence remain pending
next_action: Run the fixed-sample batch sweep on GitHub Actions; record all four throughput results and exact parity before changing the Q92 runner batch size or starting historical shards.
